pamphlet_excerpts: Galton Scientifically Prove: Galton was able to scientifically prove what Herscheland Faulds already suspected: that fingerprints are permanentand unique to each individual.
Odds Individual Fingerprints: According to Galton’s calculations, the odds of two individual fingerprints being the samewere 1 in 64 billion.
Juan Vucetich Argentine: In 1891, Juan Vucetich, an Argentine police official, began the first fingerprint files based on Galton pattern types.
Vucetich Criminal: In 1892, Vucetich made the first criminal fingerprint identification.
step_by_step_procedure: Classification System: The classification system was basedon Galton’s observations, as revised by Sir Edward Richard Henry.
New York Stateprison: In 1903, the New York Stateprison system became the first agency in the United States toregularly use fingerprints to identify criminals.
Leavenworth Bureau Became: The Leavenworth bureau became the first to operate on morethan a local basis.
Gradually Began Offer: It gradually began to offer a free fingerprintexchange service among a growing list of participating lawenforcement officers.

pamphlet_excerpts: Biometrics Our Society: Biometrics in our Society People can identify themselves for access and for privilegesin several general ways.
Token-based Identification: Token-based identification systemsinclude driver’s licenses and passports.
Knowledge-basedidentification Systems: Knowledge-basedidentification systems include a computer password, apersonal identification number, and security questions forpassword.
Biometricidentifiers Unique: Because biometricidentifiers are unique toindividuals, biometricidentification systems aremore reliable than token- orknowledge-based systems.
step_by_step_procedure: Biometrics Bodymeasurements: Biometrics are bodymeasurements used to identifypeople.
Systems Enhance Security: These systems can enhance security of access tocomputer systems and their data and to buildings, laboratories, and warehouses.
They Confirm Identity: They can confirm identity foraccess to medical records and bank accounts and for properuse of travel documents.
Computers Thousands: Using computers, thousands of comparisons per second canbe made and it is no longer necessary to limit searches to only asmall portion of the entire.

pamphlet_excerpts: Identification Friction-ridge: For an identification to be made, the friction-ridge detailsfrom two impressions must match without any unexplainabledissimilarities.
Unexplainable Difference: Even one unexplainable difference means thefingerprints are not from the same finger.
Minimum Amount Area: No minimum amount of area or minimum number offeatures or points is required to make an identification.
Area Small Tip: Often, an area as small as the tip of a pencil eraser may be identified, if the friction-ridge detail that is present is clearly represented.
step_by_step_procedure: Phone Booth Southwestern: From a phone booth in a southwestern city, a mancalled the police, asking for help.
They Tall Young: When the officersarrived, they found a tall, young, red-haired manwaiting for them.
Gun Shoulder Holsterand: He had a gun in a shoulder holsterand he told police he did not know who he was orwhere he came from.
Police Took Man: The police took the man’s fingerprints and sent them to the FBI.

Handle Fresh Work: You can handle fresh work immediately with littledanger of smudging.
Denatured Alcohol Works: Denatured alcohol works wellas a cleansing fluid. • You can get paper fingerprint cards from your localpolice department.
Ask Personalidentification: Be sure to ask for the personalidentification type.
step_by_step_procedure: Drawing Shows Sets: The drawing shows two sets of fingerprints, taken from the left hands of twodifferent people.
Loop Patterns Arch: Notice that each set has three loop patterns, one arch pattern, and one whorl, but the order of the patterns in each set is different.
Order Ofthe Patterns: The order ofthe patterns helps to identify different people.
Fingerprintingsystems Apreinked: Some fingerprintingsystems use apreinked padinstead of a rollerand inking plate.

pamphlet_excerpts: Fingerprints Classified: Fingerprints are classified into three basic types, loops, arches, and whorls, based on the patterns made by the ridges thatcover the skin.
Learning Recognize: Learning to recognize thesegeneral patterns and their subcategories is not hard.
Study Theexamples Shown: Study theexamples shown in this pamphlet, then complete the worksheetfound on page 38 to show your counselor you can identify thethree basic types.
Identify Patterntypes Own: Also identify the patterntypes of your own fingerprints.
step_by_step_procedure: Loop Pattern Ridges: In the loop pattern, the ridges begin on one side of the finger, curve or turn back sharply, and end on the same side.
Loopmay Slope Lean: The loopmay slope or “lean” toward either the thumb or the little finger.
Identify Bones Forearm: If you can identify the two bones in your forearm, theradius and ulna, then you can remember the two subcategoriesof loops.
Ridges Radial Loop: The ridges of a radial loop begin and end on the sameside of the hand as the thumb (or the radius, the bone that is onthe inside of the arm).
